title: Direct-image internal-Hom comparison on open Ext groups
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_X),D(\mathcal O_Y)$ of module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category], derived direct image $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For $E,N\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, let $c_{E,N}:Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(E,N)\to R\mathcal Hom_Y(Rf_*E,Rf_*N)$ be the canonical evaluation-mate comparison of [lem-pc-sheaf-rhom-projection-formula]. For every open $V\subseteq Y$, put $U=f^{-1}V$ and $g=f|_U:U\to V$. Under the canonical open-restriction comparisons for $Rf_*$ and $R\mathcal Hom$, the restriction of $c_{E,N}$ is $c^g_{E|_U,N|_U}$. For every integer $q$, under the canonical identifications
$$H^q(V,Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(E,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(E|_U,N|_U[q]),$$
$$H^q(V,R\mathcal Hom_Y(Rf_*E,Rf_*N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_V)}(Rg_*(E|_U),Rg_*(N|_U)[q]),$$
the map $H^q(V,c_{E,N})$ sends $u$ to $Rg_*u$, using the canonical shift comparison of the exact derived functor $Rg_*$. These identities are natural in $E,N$ and compatible with restriction to smaller opens. Here $H^q(V,A)=H^q(R\Gamma(V,A))$ [def-pc-open-module-derived-sections]. No adjunction with $Rf_*$ as left adjoint, quasi-coherence, boundedness, or compactness hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $F=Lf^*$, $G=Rf_*$, $H_T(A,B)=R\mathcal Hom_T(A,B)$, and $e_T$ for the canonical uncurrying bijection. Let $\varepsilon:FG\to1$ be the pullback/direct-image counit and $t:F(A\otimes B)\cong FA\otimes FB$ the canonical monoidal comparison. The cited comparison is characterized as follows: for $a:A\to GH_X(E,N)$ its composite with $c_{E,N}$ uncurries on $Y$ to the adjoint of
$$F(A\otimes GE)\xrightarrow{t}FA\otimes FGE\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_E}FA\otimes E\xrightarrow{e_X(\operatorname{adj}^{-1}(a))}N.$$
Indeed its evaluation transpose is relative cup product followed by $G$ of evaluation, as in Tag 0B69. Applying the adjunction formula to relative cup product gives exactly these three arrows. Thus this formula specifies the already given canonical comparison, rather than a new choice of it. The monoidal model also supplies the unit isomorphism $l:F1_Y\cong1_X$ and its unit laws.

Let $r_X,r_Y$ be restriction to $U,V$, respectively, and $F_0=Lg^*$, $G_0=Rg_*$. Use the direct-image restriction isomorphism $r_YG\cong G_0r_X$ and the internal-Hom restriction isomorphisms. Restrict the three-arrow formula of Step 1. Uncurrying commutes with restriction by the closed-monoidal restriction statement. For the canonical comparisons here, its equation is also read directly from the defining componentwise uncurrying: restriction sends $a\otimes v\mapsto\phi(a)(v)$ to the same formula on the smaller open; the unit map is likewise unchanged. This pins the comparison to the canonical internal-Hom restriction isomorphism, rather than to unspecified witnesses. For the middle arrow the cited counit equation is exactly
$$F_0(b_K);\varepsilon_{0,r_XK}=d_{GK};r_X(\varepsilon_K),$$
where $b:r_YG\cong G_0r_X$ and $d:F_0r_Y\cong r_XF$ are the canonical open comparisons (semicolon means composition in order). The first arrow also agrees: the monoidal model defines it on every K-flat tensor summand by the ordinary pullback tensor map, and restricting that map simply restricts both entries and their coefficients. The last arrow agrees by preservation of uncurrying. Substituting the counit equation therefore turns the restricted formula into precisely Step 1 for $g,E_U,N_U$. Injectivity of the adjunction and uncurrying bijections proves $r_Y(c_{E,N})=c^g_{E_U,N_U}$ with the stated source and target comparisons.

proof.text:
The natural Leray isomorphism of abelian presheaves gives
$$H^q(V,GH_X(E,N))\cong H^q(U,H_X(E,N)).$$
Apply the open Ext comparison to the right hand side to get $\operatorname{Hom}(E_U,N_U[q])$. Apply the same Ext comparison on $Y$ to $(GE,GN)$ to get $\operatorname{Hom}((GE)_V,(GN)_V[q])$, and then the direct-image restriction isomorphisms to identify this with $\operatorname{Hom}(G_0E_U,G_0N_U[q])$. These are exactly the two isomorphisms in the statement; the cited presheaf statements already include all integer degrees, naturality and smaller-open restriction compatibility. It remains to compute the map under them.

Fix the canonical degree-zero section convention. For any scheme $T$ and $B\in D(\mathcal O_T)$, a cycle $s\in\Gamma(T,I(B)^0)$ gives the chain map $1_T[0]\to I(B)$ taking $1$ to $s$. Boundaries give homotopies, and the K-injective localization bijection identifies its class with a unique arrow $\gamma_T(B)([s]):1_T\to B$. This defines the canonical section-to-unit-Hom identification.
For its compatibility with open Ext, choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $E$ using the resolution theorem, and a K-injective representative $J$ of $N$. The cited Hom theorem says $C=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J)$ is K-injective; by the definition it represents $H_T(E,N)$. Thus a class $x\in H^0(T,H_T(E,N))$ is a global degree-zero cycle $\phi$ of $C$, namely a chain map $P\to J$. The canonical Ext comparison of Tag 08DK sends $x$ to $u=Q\phi$. Meanwhile $\gamma_T(H_T(E,N))(x)$ is represented by the map $1_T[0]\to C$ taking $1$ to $\phi$. The defining componentwise uncurrying equation sends this map on the summand $1_T^0\otimes P^p$ to $a\otimes v\mapsto a\phi^p(v)$. Consequently
$$e_T(\gamma_T(H_T(E,N))(x))=u\circ\lambda_E.$$
All representatives have the hypotheses required by the cited statements. This computation fixes the canonical conventions; existence of abstract additive equivalences alone would not fix them.

We spell out the normalization needed in degree zero. For $B\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, let $x\in H^0(Y,GB)$ correspond by Leray to $y\in H^0(X,B)$. Under the canonical section-to-unit-Hom identifications, write $a:1_Y\to GB$ and $b:1_X\to B$. Then
$$\operatorname{adj}^{-1}(a)=b\circ l,\qquad a=G(b)\circ\operatorname{adj}(l).$$
Here is a representative check, avoiding any assertion that $f_*$ preserves K-injectives. Choose a K-injective representative $J$ of $B$. The cited sections-acyclicity theorem makes $\Gamma(Y,f_*J)=\Gamma(X,J)$ compute both sides of Leray. A degree-zero cycle $s$ defines the map $1_X[0]\to J$ taking $1$ to $s$; the same cycle on $Y$ defines $1_Y[0]\to f_*J$. Under the ordinary module pullback adjunction the latter transposes to the former composed with $f^*1_Y\cong1_X$. Localization yields the displayed equation for the derived adjunction: the unit sheaf in degree zero is K-flat (tensoring with it is the identity), and the target is K-injective, so the derived adjunction uses this same ordinary chain map. Boundaries are chain homotopies; the K-injective localization bijection identifies their classes. Thus this is the canonical Leray comparison, not merely some additive bijection. The section-to-Hom convention is the explicit canonical one fixed in Step 4.

proof.text:
First work over the whole spaces and with $q=0$. Put $B=H_X(E,N)$ and let the class corresponding to $u:E\to N$ give $b:1_X\to B$ and $a:1_Y\to GB$. By the canonical unit calculation of Step 4,
$$e_X(b)=u\circ\lambda_E,$$
where $\lambda_E:1_X\otimes E\cong E$. Substitute $\operatorname{adj}^{-1}(a)=b\circ l$ from Step 5 into Step 1. Naturality of uncurrying and the strong monoidal unit law reduce the adjoint's argument to
$$F(1_Y\otimes GE)\xrightarrow{F\lambda_{GE}}FGE\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_E}E\xrightarrow{u}N.$$
Counit naturality says $u\circ\varepsilon_E=\varepsilon_N\circ FG(u)$. Since $\operatorname{adj}(v)=G(v)\circ\eta$ and $G(\varepsilon_E)\circ\eta_{GE}=1_{GE}$, the adjoint of this composite is $G(u)\circ\lambda_{GE}$. Uncurrying and the canonical unit calculation on $Y$ therefore identify the output with $G(u)$. This calculation uses only the pullback-left/direct-image-right adjunction; no right adjoint of $G$ occurs.

proof.text: For arbitrary $q\in\mathbf Z$, use $H_X(E,N)[q]\cong H_X(E,N[q])$ and the analogous isomorphism on $Y$, and $G(N[q])\cong(GN)[q]$. The cited unbounded right-derived functor theorem supplies the last shift comparison; it applies both to direct image and to derived sections. The comparison $c$ respects these identifications: in its three-arrow defining formula, shift the target $N$; evaluation becomes evaluation into $N[q]$, the counit becomes its shifted counit, and the tensor comparison has unchanged source factors. Equivalently, on the Hom-complex model the degree-$q$ cocycle is the chain map to the shifted target, so this is the right-shift internal-Hom comparison. Thus the degree-$q$ map is the degree-zero calculation of Step 6 with target $N[q]$, followed by $G(N[q])\cong(GN)[q]$. It sends $u:E\to N[q]$ to $G(u)$ with exactly that shift comparison. Apply this calculation to $g$ and use Steps 2–3 to obtain the claimed formula over every $V$.

source.place: Tag 08DK (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), Tag 08DJ (lemma-internal-hom), Tag 0B69; right-shift Hom-complex construction, sites-cohomology.tex Section 0A8X

proof.text: For $t:E'\to E$, $s:N\to N'$ the represented Ext morphism is $s[q]\circ u\circ t$. Functoriality gives $G_0(s)[q]\circ G_0(u)\circ G_0(t)$ after the natural shift comparison. This proves the asserted two-variable naturality. For $W\subseteq V$, the presheaf Leray and Ext comparisons commute with restriction. The direct-image restriction isomorphism is natural in the arrow $u$, so under those comparisons restricting $Rg_*u$ is exactly $R(g|_{f^{-1}W})_*(u|_{f^{-1}W})$. For successive restrictions the sectionwise identities $f^{-1}W\subseteq f^{-1}V$ compose; restriction of a section twice is its direct restriction. The corresponding canonical derived comparisons are induced by these same identities, hence their intermediate inverse factors cancel. This gives compatibility with every smaller open, including identity and empty restrictions.
